blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-newcomer-1 (The premium test is a bit trick that does not mean "10 euros and more") is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Replace the bit trick with the rule the proposal states, behind a named constant: `const PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS = 1000;` and `p.cents >= PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS`. As written, `(cents >> 4) & 0x3e8` only tests some bits of `cents / 16` against the bit pattern of 1000: 128 cents (1.28 €) gives 8 & 1000 = 8 and lands in "hi", 999 cents gives 62 & 1000 = 40 and lands in "hi", while 16384 cents (163.84 €) gives 1024 & 1000 = 0 and lands in "lo". A reader cannot see the threshold, and the proposal's "premium products (10 euros and more)" is not what runs.
findings.title: The premium test is a bit trick that does not mean "10 euros and more"

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: Write it as a plain function: compute `isPremium(p)` once, then push into one of two arrays (or use two `filter` calls) and return them. A reduce whose callback mutates the accumulator through `||=` and returns it via a comma operator has to be decoded token by token; the simple version wins and costs nothing here.
findings.title: `bucket` is a dense one-liner with a comma expression and `||=` inside an index

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: Name the function after what it does (`splitByPriceBand`, or `partitionPremium`), the parameter `prices`, and use keys that match the doc comment and the domain (`cheap` / `premium`) instead of the magic strings "hi" / "lo".
findings.title: Names say nothing: `bucket`, `ps`, `a`, `p`, `"hi"` / `"lo"`

findings.recommendation: Declare the result as `{ cheap: Price[]; premium: Price[] }` and always initialise both arrays. Today a caller reading the signature cannot know the keys are "hi" and "lo", and when no price falls in a band the key is missing, so `bucket(prices).hi` is `undefined` while the type claims `Price[]`.
findings.title: The return type `Record<string, Price[]>` hides its two keys and their possible absence

findings.evidence: - [x] 1.1 `bucket`, verified by the catalogue page, where premium products are listed apart
findings.recommendation: Add a test that reads as the behavior: "a price of 999 cents is cheap", "a price of 1000 cents is premium", "a price of 16384 cents is premium", "an empty list gives two empty bands". Such a test would have caught R-newcomer-1.
findings.title: No test describes the split; the only verification is looking at a page
